messages:
Matt: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in GPU OOMs on the canary after the kernel-selector change. Suspect interaction between subkeying for batching and KV cache TTL/eviction.

Jess: Which canary/PR? link?

Matt: PR is https://git.redwood/infra/ker-sel-v2 (canary tag). Quick profiler dump:
```
GPU0 kv_slots_total: 100k
used_slots: 88k
free_slots: 12k
frag_ratio: 0.47
avg_slot_size: 2.3MB
compaction_events: 6 (last 10m)
unique_key_rate: +3.1x vs baseline
```

Anya: Did we change key normalization or hashing? Small changes there can blow up unique-key counts.

Leo: We added subkeying that splits long prefixes into 128B subkeys to improve kernel batching across requests. It reduces batch variance but increases cardinality.

Sylvia: Oof. That can turn a prefix that used to hit into many short keys that never aggregate -> fragmentation + compaction storms. Suggest TTL-hysteresis + probabilistic eviction as a quick mitigation.

Matt: Did two quick experiments locally:
```
Experiment A: disable subkeying -> unique_key_rate down 3x, peak GPU mem stable
Experiment B: keep subkeying + bump soft_cap by 15% + coalesce windows -> peak mem -22%, average latency +10ms
```

InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary "kernel-sel-v2" rolled back automatically after 4 OOMs within 30m. Incident ticket #INC-4632 created.

Jess: Action list I propose: 1) revert subkeying in canary immediately, 2) implement TTL hysteresis + probabilistic eviction for prefill cohort, 3) add per-GPU entropy/heatmap dashboard to console, 4) add warmup jitter/backoff for prefill to avoid synchronized compaction.

Leo: I'll open a revert PR and a separate mitigation PR for probabilistic eviction (sampler-based). Metric PR coming: unique_key_rate, frag_ratio, slot_compaction_events, prefill_storm_count.

Anya: For TTL hysteresis: idea is soft-ttl that extends life for keys with repeated hits within window, but decays faster for one-off keys. Implementation: keep a small hit-counter + last-hit timestamp per key and compute effective-ttl = base_ttl + alpha * min(hit_count, max_hysteresis) with sampling.

Sylvia: Also recommend changing compaction trigger to avoid global full-slab compactions: prefer incremental slab compaction on low-util GPUs first, and rate-limit compaction_tasks per-region.

Matt: Agree. Also want to add a "subkey collapse" pass in runtime: when a parent prefix is seen to have high local hit-rate, collapse subkeys into parent entry for 30s to reclaim slots. Low-cost heuristic.

Leo: Good idea. I'll prototype collapse + add unit tests for key-entropy regression.

Anya: Can we add a small test harness that replays production prefix traces with and without subkeying to estimate frag_ratio and compaction events? Would help baseline decisions.

Matt: On it — I'll export a 1h sample trace from canary and run the replay. Plan: meet 1pm in #eng-runtime to triage and assign owners.

Sylvia: Thanks all. Priorities: revert -> metrics -> mitigation.

InfraBot: reminder: incident #INC-4632 linked to ticket https://inc.redwood/4632 - please update status after revert.
